s1.quote: This cenote is around 60 meters deep in places. … it is only suitable for advanced open water divers or those with deep certification.

s2.quote: Thirty feet below, brown hydrogen sulfide is forever trapped … intersect with the floor at a maximum depth of 203 feet.

highlights.text: Hydrogen sulfide cloud hovering above the floor

summary.text: A deep cenote in Quintana Roo where a layer of hydrogen sulfide forms a misty cloud over the bottom. Reserved for advanced or deep-certified divers because of the depths involved.

s1.quote: The dive follows the course of the river at a depth of no more than 8m. … Due to the connection with the ocean, both fresh and saltwater fish live there.

s2.quote: depth is around 6-8 m or 20-25 ft

highlights.text: Mangrove roots overhead, fresh and salt water fish

summary.text: A shallow, calm dive along a mangrove-fringed channel that links the cenote to the sea near Tulum. Easy conditions suit beginners, with small fish among the roots and a cave line leading into the dark.
